## Implementation notes

- **Fail-closed Miami.** AOS000960's Miami PD row binds two live
  `deployment_exists`/`Face Recognition` claims to the same evidence
  captures; the upstream AOS row cannot be joined to one claim from
  committed data alone. `candidate_claim_ids` suppresses BOTH claims
  until the host-side rerun narrows them (D-P34.19-1 step 2 — the
  AOS005165-linked claim is NOT to be dispositioned). Fail closed:
  over-suppress one possibly-clean claim (a candidate) rather than leak
  a tainted row.
- **Entity-level semantics.** The withdrawal's public-artifact
  semantics are "suppress matching claims AND their subject entities":
  `_apply_publication_withdrawals` drops any claim whose `subject_id`
  is a withdrawn entity (an early draft matched claim ids only — a
  withdrawn entity's coordinate/jurisdiction claims still leaked;
  caught by the export test, fixed).
- **Both seams.** `build_spine_export` filters `claims` (sites,
  record claims, tiles, search derive from it) and `dataset.sites`
  (map, dossiers, coverage, analytics derive from it) BEFORE any
  surface builds — one suppression point keeps every artifact
  consistent. Dropped claims are recorded loudly in `exclusions.json`
  (`withdrawn` + `withdrawn_claims` total), never silently, never an
  `UPDATE`/`DELETE`.
- **Additive compat.** New `RightsRecord` fields default `""`; older
  fixtures/callers unchanged. The PG path decorates via
  `policy.disclosure.apply_to_record` rather than widening the SELECT —
  the hosted schema predate the columns, so the read stays
  old-schema-safe (read-only).
- **JSON data tables.** `policy._data.load_json_table` added because
  verbatim captures carry embedded markup/quotes and the TypeScript
  layer must read the same bytes without a TOML dependency — the
  disclosure + withdrawal lists stay data (SIG-LIC-004a), not code.
- **Honest absence.** `web/terms_disclosure.json` and each
  `ATTRIBUTION.json` are emitted only when the export actually carries
  affected rows (scoped exports emit none); `getTermsDisclosure()`
  reads a missing artifact as an empty source list — never a
  fabricated entry.

## Self-review

**Pass 1 — mechanical.** Per-file diff walk: `sources.toml` is exactly
eight additive rights-block extensions (3 fields + comment each;
`ingestion_permitted`, `rights_reviewed_by/on`, dated `notes`
byte-identical); `rights.py`/`registry.py`/`licensing.py` additive
optional fields; `store_pg.py` decorates rather than widening the
SELECT (old-schema-safe); `spine_export.py` adds the withdrawal seam +
two artifact emitters and threads `withdrawn_entities` into the map
exclude + exclusions.json; `data.ts` filters export-mode payloads
through the shared list and adds `getTermsDisclosure`; DEFERRALS +
batch-01 + events.jsonl appended only; projection regenerated by its
tool. `git status` confirms no stray/generated edits; `.env`,
`docs/build/logs/` untouched.

**Pass 2 — design.** The two design faults found by the tests — (a)
claim-id-only matching leaked a withdrawn entity's
coordinate/jurisdiction claims, fixed by entity-level suppression in
`_apply_publication_withdrawals`; (b) the first draft read site rows
from `web_artifacts` while they live in the bundle artifact bytes —
are exactly the failure class the ticket's "0 of nine rows in every
public artifact" criterion targets. Miami's two-claim ambiguity is
resolved fail-closed (`candidate_claim_ids` suppresses the candidate
alongside the target) with the narrowing recorded as a named
rerun step in D-P34.19-1 rather than guessed — the withdrawal
deliberately over-suppresses one claim rather than risk a tainted row.
The disclosure counts are computed from each export's own slices
(`export_row_count`) so a scoped export reports its own truth, while
`public_row_count` in the policy table is the acceptance-basis number
(8,088) — two different honest numbers, each labelled.
